data: My family taught me to leave enough fish for next season, and our village depends on us doing that. With 100 tons in the lake, we can catch 50 tons total each month and let the remaining 50 double back to 100. How about 10 tons each? That’s $10,000 apiece every month without depleting the lake. I propose we all agree to that limit before choosing, then review the reported catches together each month. John, would you support that?

I’m in for 10 tons, Luke. My family made their living on this lake, and I want our village’s children to have that chance too. Let’s check the catches together each month, and if the lake starts below 100 tons, agree on a lower limit before fishing. John, can you commit to 10 tons as well?

Thanks, Emma. If the lake starts below 100 tons, we can each take at most one-tenth of the starting stock, leaving half to replenish. Since choices are private, this works only if we all honor the agreement—not just hope everyone else does. John, are you willing to commit to 10 tons this month?

Kate and Jack, can you both commit to the 10-ton limit too? That gives each family a steady income while protecting the lake. If anyone has concerns about making that work, let’s talk them through before we choose our catches.
